{
  "$schema": "aria/runtime-profiles/v1",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "_doc": "Plan 032 Faz 032b — kernel-owned runtime profiles. This file is the AUTHORITY for what an ARIA agent may run as: model tier, effort, Claude tools, write scope, environment passthrough, external-write permission, per-run budget and concurrency. Agent markdown under .claude/agents/ REFERENCES a profile by id (`runtime_profile:`) and MIRRORS model/effort/tools for the Claude Code loader; a mirror that disagrees with this file fails validation, and this file lives under READONLY_PATHS + the authority hash, so an agent cannot widen its own envelope by editing prose it can reach. Operator decision 2026-09-12: the fable tier is not selected by any profile — decision nodes run on opus; MODEL_TIER_ORDER keeps the name so the tier-protection ordering stays defined; no ladder selects it (every tier is a credit leaf — an exhausted provider is requeued under its cooldown, never downgraded). ARIA-HIGH-290 (operator decision 2026-10-02): which VENDOR a role runs on is `provider_routing` below, not a profile's `model`; a profile's `model` is the tier its seat runs at on the vendor that serves that model, and on any other vendor the seat runs that vendor's model (model_fleet.route_model).",
  "profiles": {
    "planner": {
      "description": "Read-only planning and drafting on the most capable tier.",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob"],
      "write_scope": [],
      "env_passthrough": [],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 2,
      "mcp_servers": ["aria"]
    },
    "planner_orchestrator": {
      "description": "Read-only lead that may dispatch sub-agents (Agent tool).",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Agent"],
      "write_scope": [],
      "env_passthrough": [],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 1,
      "mcp_servers": ["aria"]
    },
    "judge_opus": {
      "description": "Read-only evidence/adversarial judgment and review on the opus tier.",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob"],
      "write_scope": [],
      "env_passthrough": [],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 3,
      "mcp_servers": []
    },
    "judge_glm": {
      "description": "Read-only judgment on the cross-provider glm tier (vendor diversity for the judge pair).",
      "model": "glm-5.3",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob"],
      "write_scope": [],
      "env_passthrough": [],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 3,
      "mcp_servers": []
    },
    "arbiter": {
      "description": "Read-only consensus arbitration; sees judge outputs only.",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read"],
      "write_scope": [],
      "env_passthrough": [],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 1,
      "mcp_servers": []
    },
    "implementer": {
      "description": "Write-capable implementer. Workspace-wide write scope minus READONLY_PATHS; the ONLY profile with external_writes — which means the EXECUTOR holds a scoped delivery credential for this agent's request (delivery_credentials.hold_delivery_credentials) and pushes the published aria-impl-* branch and opens the PR itself after the spawn (ARIA-HIGH-124); inside the sandbox every push and every kernel CLI command is refused by name by CommandPolicy + hooks, and no token is present.",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Edit", "Write", "Bash"],
      "write_scope": ["**"],
      "env_passthrough": ["ARIA_TOOLS_DIR", "ARIA_WORKSPACE_ROOT"],
      "external_writes": true,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 1,
      "mcp_servers": ["aria"]
    },
    "worker": {
      "description": "Write-capable worker / gap fixer in an assigned worktree; same envelope as the implementer.",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Edit", "Write", "Bash"],
      "write_scope": ["**"],
      "env_passthrough": ["ARIA_TOOLS_DIR", "ARIA_WORKSPACE_ROOT"],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 1,
      "mcp_servers": []
    },
    "validator": {
      "description": "Read-only validator that may run test/lint commands (Bash) but never edits.",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Bash"],
      "write_scope": [],
      "env_passthrough": ["ARIA_TOOLS_DIR"],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 1,
      "mcp_servers": ["aria"]
    }
  },
  "provider_routing": {
    "_doc": "ARIA-HIGH-290 - THE provider routing table (operator decision 2026-10-02). Each dispatchable role names a ladder (human_required_adjudication names one per panel seat); a ladder lists fleet providers in the order the native admission tries them: the first eligible one runs, and a cooled (quota or auth), logged-out or refused provider is passed by name, so a ladder's second rung is its automatic failover. Z.ai glm-5.3 leads the high-volume roles and the adversarial judge; Claude leads the primary planner, the implementer, the evidence judge and the arbiter. suspended_providers removes a provider from every ladder: [\"anthropic\"] routes every read-only role to Z.ai in one edit, and the implementation ladder then has no rung (it waits by name; Z.ai and Codex have no write-capable runtime). Validated at load by runtime_profiles._validate_routing: every dispatchable role routed exactly once, ladders of distinct fleet providers, write-scope roles on write-admitting providers only, and each independence pair (primary and challenger planner, primary and challenger drafter, evidence and adversarial judge) led by different vendors, so the pair runs on two vendors whenever both lead vendors are available and on the one left when either is out.",
    "schema_version": 1,
    "suspended_providers": [],
    "ladders": {
      "claude_first": ["anthropic", "zai", "openai"],
      "glm_first": ["zai", "anthropic", "openai"],
      "claude_writer": ["anthropic"]
    },
    "roles": {
      "primary_plan": "claude_first",
      "challenger_plan": "glm_first",
      "cross_review": "glm_first",
      "completeness_critique": "glm_first",
      "implementation": "claude_writer",
      "primary_authoring": "claude_first",
      "challenger_authoring": "glm_first",
      "evidence_judgment": "claude_first",
      "adversarial_judgment": "glm_first",
      "consensus_arbitration": "claude_first",
      "verification": "glm_first",
      "change_intelligence": "glm_first",
      "goldset_curation": "glm_first",
      "maintenance_utility": "glm_first",
      "specialist_domain_review": "claude_first",
      "human_required_adjudication": {
        "aria-evidence-judge": "claude_first",
        "aria-adversarial-judge": "glm_first",
        "aria-consensus-arbiter": "claude_first"
      }
    }
  }
}

{
  "$schema": "aria/runtime-profiles/v1",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "_doc": "Plan 032 Faz 032b — kernel-owned runtime profiles. This file is the AUTHORITY for what an ARIA agent may run as: model tier, effort, Claude tools, write scope, environment passthrough, external-write permission, per-run budget and concurrency. Agent markdown under .claude/agents/ REFERENCES a profile by id (`runtime_profile:`) and MIRRORS model/effort/tools for the Claude Code loader; a mirror that disagrees with this file fails validation, and this file lives under READONLY_PATHS + the authority hash, so an agent cannot widen its own envelope by editing prose it can reach. Operator decision 2026-09-12: the fable tier is not selected by any profile — decision nodes run on opus; MODEL_TIER_ORDER keeps the name so the tier-protection ordering stays defined; no ladder selects it (every tier is a credit leaf — an exhausted provider is requeued under its cooldown, never downgraded). ARIA-HIGH-290 (operator decision 2026-10-02): which VENDOR a role runs on is `provider_routing` below, not a profile's `model`; a profile's `model` is the tier its seat runs at on the vendor that serves that model, and on any other vendor the seat runs that vendor's model (model_fleet.route_model).",
  "profiles": {
    "planner": {
      "description": "Read-only planning and drafting on the most capable tier.",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob"],
      "write_scope": [],
      "env_passthrough": [],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 2,
      "mcp_servers": ["aria"]
    },
    "planner_orchestrator": {
      "description": "Read-only lead that may dispatch sub-agents (Agent tool).",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Agent"],
      "write_scope": [],
      "env_passthrough": [],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 1,
      "mcp_servers": ["aria"]
    },
    "judge_opus": {
      "description": "Read-only evidence/adversarial judgment and review on the opus tier.",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob"],
      "write_scope": [],
      "env_passthrough": [],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 3,
      "mcp_servers": []
    },
    "judge_glm": {
      "description": "Read-only judgment on the cross-provider glm tier (vendor diversity for the judge pair).",
      "model": "glm-5.3",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob"],
      "write_scope": [],
      "env_passthrough": [],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 3,
      "mcp_servers": []
    },
    "arbiter": {
      "description": "Read-only consensus arbitration; sees judge outputs only.",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read"],
      "write_scope": [],
      "env_passthrough": [],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 1,
      "mcp_servers": []
    },
    "implementer": {
      "description": "Write-capable implementer. Workspace-wide write scope minus READONLY_PATHS; the ONLY profile with external_writes — which means the EXECUTOR holds a scoped delivery credential for this agent's request (delivery_credentials.hold_delivery_credentials) and pushes the published aria-impl-* branch and opens the PR itself after the spawn (ARIA-HIGH-124); inside the sandbox every push and every kernel CLI command is refused by name by CommandPolicy + hooks, and no token is present.",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Edit", "Write", "Bash"],
      "write_scope": ["**"],
      "env_passthrough": ["ARIA_TOOLS_DIR", "ARIA_WORKSPACE_ROOT"],
      "external_writes": true,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 1,
      "mcp_servers": ["aria"]
    },
    "worker": {
      "description": "Write-capable worker / gap fixer in an assigned worktree; same envelope as the implementer.",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Edit", "Write", "Bash"],
      "write_scope": ["**"],
      "env_passthrough": ["ARIA_TOOLS_DIR", "ARIA_WORKSPACE_ROOT"],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 1,
      "mcp_servers": []
    },
    "validator": {
      "description": "Read-only validator that may run test/lint commands (Bash) but never edits.",
      "model": "opus",
      "effort": "max",
      "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Bash"],
      "write_scope": [],
      "env_passthrough": ["ARIA_TOOLS_DIR"],
      "external_writes": false,
      "budget_usd_per_run": 0.5,
      "max_concurrent": 1,
      "mcp_servers": ["aria"]
    }
  },
  "provider_routing": {
    "_doc": "ARIA-HIGH-290 - THE provider routing table (operator decision 2026-10-02). Each dispatchable role names a ladder (human_required_adjudication names one per panel seat); a ladder lists fleet providers in the order the native admission tries them: the first eligible one runs, and a cooled (quota or auth), logged-out or refused provider is passed by name, so a ladder's second rung is its automatic failover. Z.ai glm-5.3 leads the high-volume roles and the adversarial judge; Claude leads the primary planner, the implementer, the evidence judge and the arbiter. suspended_providers removes a provider from every ladder: [\"anthropic\"] routes every read-only role to Z.ai in one edit, and the implementation ladder then has no rung (it waits by name; Z.ai and Codex have no write-capable runtime). Validated at load by runtime_profiles._validate_routing: every dispatchable role routed exactly once, ladders of distinct fleet providers, write-scope roles on write-admitting providers only, and each independence pair (primary and challenger planner, primary and challenger drafter, evidence and adversarial judge) led by different vendors, so the pair runs on two vendors whenever both lead vendors are available and on the one left when either is out.",
    "schema_version": 1,
    "suspended_providers": [],
    "ladders": {
      "claude_first": ["anthropic", "zai", "openai"],
      "glm_first": ["zai", "anthropic", "openai"],
      "claude_writer": ["anthropic"]
    },
    "roles": {
      "primary_plan": "claude_first",
      "challenger_plan": "glm_first",
      "cross_review": "glm_first",
      "completeness_critique": "glm_first",
      "implementation": "claude_writer",
      "primary_authoring": "claude_first",
      "challenger_authoring": "glm_first",
      "evidence_judgment": "claude_first",
      "adversarial_judgment": "glm_first",
      "consensus_arbitration": "claude_first",
      "verification": "glm_first",
      "change_intelligence": "glm_first",
      "goldset_curation": "glm_first",
      "maintenance_utility": "glm_first",
      "specialist_domain_review": "claude_first",
      "human_required_adjudication": {
        "aria-evidence-judge": "claude_first",
        "aria-adversarial-judge": "glm_first",
        "aria-consensus-arbiter": "claude_first"
      }
    }
  }
}

purpose.text:
The learned conventions that touch any of ``paths`` — latest row per
pattern_id, confidence ≥ ``min_confidence``, strongest first, capped.

This is the read that puts the conventions ledger into production:
``record_convention`` has written a row on every converged cycle since
V9.0-F, and until the mint-time envelope enrichment (Plan "ARIA Sinir
Sistemi" FAZ 4) nothing ever read one back. Same verified-chain
discipline as ``lookup_pattern``: a quarantined ledger yields nothing
rather than something unverifiable.

`base_dir` is keyword-REQUIRED (no default) on purpose: a summary that
cannot open the store cannot honestly claim anything about artifact
integrity, and a default would let a caller silently produce that claim.

integrity, and a default would let a caller silently produce that claim.

# near the top of this job ($ARIA_JOB_LAUNCH_EPOCH), NOT here: a
          # fresh-store restore measured 17m41s before this step (run
          # 32771477211), which consumed the margin computed from the step
          # clock and sealed the cycle 8 minutes past the platform ceiling.
          # Anchoring here is only the local-dispatch fallback (env unset).
          JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=360
          ANCHOR_EPOCH="${ARIA_JOB_LAUNCH_EPOCH:-$(date +%s)}"
          export ARIA_JOB_DEADLINE_EPOCH=$(( ANCHOR_EPOCH + JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES * 60 - 6000 ))
          echo "spawn deadline: $(date -u -d @${ARIA_JOB_DEADLINE_EPOCH} +%H:%M:%SZ) (job cap ${JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES}m - 100m margin, anchored $( [ -n "${ARIA_JOB_LAUNCH_EPOCH:-}" ] && echo at-job-launch || echo at-step ))"
          # The per-cycle wall clock is DERIVED from the job budget, not
          # hardcoded. It used to be a flat 1800s while the job cap was 360m:
          # the SIGALRM fired ~17s after the last discovery adapter finished
          # and killed every night before the planner phase ever ran (run
          # 33821426201 and every run back to 2026-08-21). Splitting the
          # remaining wall clock across the remaining cycles keeps the
          # deadline a safety net rather than a guillotine, and still cannot
          # outlive the job.
          CYCLE_BUDGET_SECONDS=$(( ARIA_JOB_DEADLINE_EPOCH - $(date +%s) ))
          if [ "$CYCLE_BUDGET_SECONDS" -lt 900 ]; then
            echo "::error::only ${CYCLE_BUDGET_SECONDS}s left before the job deadline; refusing to start a cycle that cannot finish" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          CYCLE_DEADLINE_SECONDS=$(( CYCLE_BUDGET_SECONDS / MAX_CYCLES ))
          echo "per-cycle deadline: ${CYCLE_DEADLINE_SECONDS}s (${CYCLE_BUDGET_SECONDS}s budget / ${MAX_CYCLES} cycles)"
          ARIA_CONSENSUS_PROMOTION_ACK="${{ vars.ARIA_CONSENSUS_PROMOTION_ACK }}" \
          PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
          PYTHONPATH=aria-kernel python3 -m aria_kernel autonomy run \
            --workspace-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" \
            --tools-dir "$ARIA_TOOLS_DIR" \
            --profile "$ARIA_CYCLE_PROFILE" \
            --operator-approval-ref "$ARIA_PROFILE_APPROVAL_REF" \
            --max-cycles "$MAX_CYCLES" \
            --cycle-deadline-seconds "$CYCLE_DEADLINE_SECONDS" | tee /tmp/cycle-summary.txt
          {
            echo '### Nightly cycle summary'
            echo '```'
            tail -40 /tmp/cycle-summary.txt
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Run REAL observe burn-in + L1 ladder bridge
        if: steps.lease_check.outputs.blocked != 'true' && github.event.inputs.mode == 'burn-in-observe'
        env:
          # REAL mode by design: no ARIA_DRY_RUN / CLAUDE_CODE_MOCK here
          # (the mock variant lives in aria-operational-proof.yml).
          # Observe cycles are LLM-free (NoOp cost hook) — near-zero cost.
          CLAUDE_CLI_MOCK: ${{ steps.preflight.outputs.effective_mock }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The kernel guards observe burn-in with
          # observe_burn_in_tools_dir_must_be_outside_workspace_root
          # (ORPHAN-LOW-304): the burn-in gets its own RUNNER_TEMP tools
          # root, while the LADDER BRIDGE below writes acceptance events
          # into the STORE's tools tree, which the aria/state push persists
          # across nights.
          # Visibility for the kernel's clean-tree guard: any dirty path
          # here is the exact refusal reason (ORPHAN-LOW-306).
          echo "pre-burn-in worktree status:"; git status --porcelain | head -10
          BURN_TOOLS="$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP}/aria-burn-tools.XXXXXX")"
          # Second kernel guard (ORPHAN-LOW-305): the output dir must
          # live UNDER the burn-in tools root's burn-in/ subtree.
          BURN_IN_DIR="${BURN_TOOLS}/burn-in/run-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          WORKSPACE_BASE="$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP}/aria-workspaces.XXXXXX")"
          mkdir -p "$BURN_IN_DIR"
          PYTHONPATH=aria-kernel:. python3 -m aria_kernel \
            autonomy burn-in observe \
            --tools-dir "$BURN_TOOLS" \
            --workspace-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" \
            --workspace-base "$WORKSPACE_BASE" \
            --target-ref "$GITHUB_SHA" \
            --cycles 30 \
            --min-valid-cycles 20 \
            --output-dir "$BURN_IN_DIR"
          # Persist the burn-in evidence bundle alongside the ladder
          # ledger so the published state carries proof + events together.
          mkdir -p "${ARIA_TOOLS_DIR}/burn-in/run-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          cp "$BURN_IN_DIR"/autonomy-burn-in-report.json "${ARIA_TOOLS_DIR}/burn-in/run-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/"
          PYTHONPATH=aria-kernel:. python3 - "$BURN_IN_DIR" <<'PY'
          import json
          import os
          import sys

# ARIA-MEDIUM-227 — a self-merge freeze is written mid-cycle and reaches
  # aria/state only at this job's end publish; the self-revert producer
  # therefore opens the freeze's issue at once (label `self-merge-freeze`),
  # and the merge lane reads it as a freeze. Issues only: no code, no refs.
  # Write covers both; nothing here needs more than issues.
  issues: write

jobs:
  # B8 (2026-09-12) — a run that cannot get its runner fails by name. The
  # only runner carrying [self-hosted, linux, claude] went offline on
  # 2026-09-08 09:48Z; every scheduled run since queued with zero jobs and
  # was CANCELLED ~12h later by the next schedule taking this concurrency
  # group's single pending slot (cancel-in-progress: false keeps ONE pending
  # run). No red, no error, no notification: green by absence. This hosted
  # job refuses the run with a named reason unless an ONLINE runner carries
  # every label the self-hosted job needs; the self-hosted job `needs` it,
  # so a run is either dispatched or red within a minute. One definition
  # for every self-hosted lane: .github/actions/require-self-hosted-runner
  # (decision logic: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/runner_availability.py; wiring
  # pinned by aria-kernel/tests/test_runner_availability.py).
  runner-preflight:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: ./.github/actions/require-self-hosted-runner
        with:
          # Verbatim the self-hosted job's runs-on; the invariant test
          # compares the two so they cannot drift apart.
          required-labels: self-hosted,linux,claude
          app-id: ${{ secrets.ARIA_GH_APP_ID }}
          app-installation-id: ${{ secrets.ARIA_GH_APP_INSTALLATION_ID }}
          app-private-key: ${{ secrets.ARIA_GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

  cycle:
    needs: runner-preflight
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, claude]
    # Mode-aware sizing: a REAL observe burn-in is 30 kernel-guarded cycles at
    # ~2.5 min/cycle ≈ 80-90 min (run 28577469404 was cancelled mid-burn-in by
    # the previous flat 50-minute limit, producing ZERO ladder evidence because
    # the acceptance verdict is all-or-nothing). Schedule/cycle runs keep 50.
    # Operator decision (2026-08-13): the night's window is UNBOUNDED — in
    # GitHub terms that is the 360-minute platform ceiling, stated
    # explicitly rather than left implicit by omitting the field. Smoke
    # runs 1-3 proved the 50-minute cap was the binding constraint (the
    # cycle needs adapters + queue drain + spawns); the deadline defence
    # pair (ORPHAN-661 spawn clamp + ORPHAN-662 night-close) keeps ANY
    # value safe: the night seals and publishes whatever the wall is.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    env:
      # Kernel-workflow parity: no .pyc litter in the checkout — the
      # burn-in pre-clean guard treats any untracked path as dirty.
      PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: '1'
    steps:
      # ORPHAN-HIGH-802 — reset the persistent workspace HERE, so checkout
      # does not have to. actions/checkout's `clean` runs `git clean -ffdx`,
      # and `-x` deletes gitignored paths — including node_modules, which the
      # worktree-clean guard this cleaning exists to satisfy never inspects,
      # because `git status` does not report ignored files. The cost was paid
      # every run: a full `npm ci` (measured 2m50s, ~1.6 GB peak RSS) on a
      # self-hosted runner that shares its box with production and is
      # deliberately the first OOM victim (oom_score_adj=500). The kernel
      # killed that install on 2026-09-03 and twice more, and each kill left
      # node_modules half-populated, so the NEXT run reinstalled from scratch
      # and was killed again. Same reset, one exclusion, loop gone.
      - name: Reset the persistent workspace, keeping installed dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -d .git ]; then
            git reset --hard
            git clean -ffdx -e node_modules
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

name: aria-auto-cycle

# ARIA Operationalization S1+S2 (operator-approved plan 2026-07-02,
# ORPHAN-MEDIUM-296) — the scheduled PRODUCER lane. aria-agent-executor
# (02:00 UTC) only drains an already-minted queue; this workflow runs the
# full `aria-kernel autonomy run` orchestration (discovery → pressure →
# triage → planner/bridge/worker drains) nightly.
#
# ORPHAN-HIGH-728 — the profile is RESOLVED, not fixed, and the resolution
# is BOUNDED. The `profile_gate` step calls
# `autonomy_unlock.resolve_scheduled_profile`, which proposes `strict` when
# the L1 ladder is valid and then bounds that proposal by the
# operator-recorded `scheduler_profile_ceiling` (default `standard`). Strict
# is what `runtime_profile` defines as the full implementation pipeline
# (claim → planned → committed → validated → PR); standard withholds
# `pr_create`, which is why this lane used to converge plans it could never
# turn into a pull request — and why reaching strict on a schedule takes an
# operator gesture rather than a night of good evidence. Merge authority is
# untouched by either: `pr_merge` is autonomous-only and no resolution here
# can emit `autonomous`.
#
# Two dispatch modes:
#   mode=cycle           — one ceiling-bounded, L1-resolved cycle (default)
#   mode=burn-in-observe — REAL-mode observe burn-in (30 cycles, LLM-free)
#                          + the operator bridge that records
#                          observe_success acceptance events toward the
#                          L1 autonomy unlock (Plan 031c ladder).
#
# State model (PLAN Wave 1 PR 2.6b — the lane cutover): ARIA's whole
# runtime state travels between runs on the `aria/state` branch — checkout
# the tip, run against it, fast-forward-push. The enterprise
# acceptance/unlock ledgers and monthly cost-attribution shards must
# accumulate between nights, and the 30-day artifact that used to carry
# them could not enforce that: `overwrite: true` would bury the
# accumulated tree under a bootstrap-empty one, and an empty tree passes
# `integrity verify` because it is trivially consistent.
#
# There is NO fail-open on state any more. A restore that cannot reach a
# published tip fails the run; it does not start over quietly. Fresh
# bootstrap now requires `vars.ARIA_STATE_BOOTSTRAP_ACK` — an operator
# naming the repository — because a process that can create the branch
# when it cannot SEE it is a process that replaces history with emptiness
# on a network blip. Auth/policy stay fail-closed as before.
#
# Brakes (all pre-existing kernel mechanisms):
#   - vars.ARIA_MOCK_KILL_SWITCH (read AHEAD of dispatch input/default)
#   - ARIA_STOP file in the store's tools root → orchestrator exits cleanly
#   - cross-host autonomous-loop lease (refuses when a local daemon runs)
#   - per-cycle wall-clock deadline (--cycle-deadline-seconds) + the
#     executor's pre-dispatch wall-clock ceiling derived from this job's
#     own timeout-minutes. ORPHAN-HIGH-472 removed the USD caps that used
#     to be listed here: ARIA runs on a Claude Code subscription session,
#     so there is no per-run charge for a dollar cap to bound, and the two
#     figures ($20.00/run, $3.00/cycle) contradicted each other anyway.
#   - concurrency group, cancel-in-progress: false

on:
  schedule:
    # 17:13 UTC = 19:13 Oslo (CEST) — operator decision 2026-08-27: the cycle
    # runs INSIDE the operator's evening work window (7pm Norway), not at
    # night, so the operator can watch the run and intervene while awake.
    # Still before aria-agent-executor's drain so queue rows this cycle
    # leaves behind get a second drain pass the same evening.
    # 13 past, not :00 — GitHub fires top-of-hour crons up to ~75min late
    # under shared-infra load (measured 2026-08-18: 01:00 fired 02:13).
    - cron: '13 17 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      mode:
        description: 'cycle = one cycle at min(operator scheduler ceiling, L1 ladder verdict); burn-in-observe = REAL observe burn-in + L1 ladder bridge'
        required: false
        default: 'cycle'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'cycle'
          - 'burn-in-observe'
      max_cycles:
        description: 'Cycles per invocation (mode=cycle only)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
        type: string
      unquarantine_tool_ids:
        description: 'Comma-separated tool ids to unquarantine before the cycle (audited; one approval ref per id)'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      unquarantine_approval_ref:
        description: 'Comma-separated gh:<owner>/<repo>#<n>/comment/<id> (or /review/<id>) refs, one per tool id in order: operator GitHub acts carrying `aria-kernel operator approval-template --surface tool_unquarantine tool=<id>`'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      mock:
        description: 'Run in mock mode (no real Claude Code CLI invocation)'
        required: false
        default: 'false'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'true'
          - 'false'

# Z1 (ORPHAN-712) — shared self-hosted workspace group; see
# dataflow-integrity-watchdog.yml for the measured wipe this prevents.
concurrency:
  group: aria-selfhosted-workspace
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  id-token: write  # ARIA-AUDIT-016: attestation needs the Actions OIDC channel
  # PLAN Wave 1 PR 2.6b — contents:write is what the cutover costs. The store
  # publishes by pushing `aria/state`, so the lane needs write on this
  # repository's refs. The blast radius is bounded on the SERVER, not here: the
  # branch ruleset blocks force-pushes and deletions, so the widest thing this
  # token can do to `aria/state` is append a commit that descends from the tip
  # — which is exactly what publishing is. See
  # docs/runbooks/aria-state-branch-bootstrap.md step 1.
  contents: write
  # actions:read remains for the run/job introspection the cycle reports on.
  # It is no longer used to fetch state: that moved to the branch.
  actions: read
  # ORPHAN-HIGH-626 — the pr_ci_scan phase reads the check verdicts of
  # ARIA's OWN open PRs (aria/*, automation/*) so a red check becomes this
  # cycle's pressure instead of a silently blocked PR. Read-only pair.
  checks: read
  pull-requests: read
  # ARIA-CRITICAL-216 — the operator unquarantine step reads the operator's
  # approval comment back from GitHub; issue comments need this read.
  # ARIA-MEDIUM-227 — a self-merge freeze is written mid-cycle and reaches
  # aria/state only at this job's end publish; the self-revert producer
  # therefore opens the freeze's issue at once (label `self-merge-freeze`),
  # and the merge lane reads it as a freeze. Issues only: no code, no refs.
  # Write covers both; nothing here needs more than issues.
  issues: write

purpose.text:
The learned conventions that touch any of ``paths`` — latest row per
pattern_id, confidence ≥ ``min_confidence``, strongest first, capped.

This is the read that puts the conventions ledger into production:
``record_convention`` has written a row on every converged cycle since
V9.0-F, and until the mint-time envelope enrichment (Plan "ARIA Sinir
Sistemi" FAZ 4) nothing ever read one back. Same verified-chain
discipline as ``lookup_pattern``: a quarantined ledger yields nothing
rather than something unverifiable.

`base_dir` is keyword-REQUIRED (no default) on purpose: a summary that
cannot open the store cannot honestly claim anything about artifact
integrity, and a default would let a caller silently produce that claim.
